options.content:
Health of the **@gardenio Jira conversational bridge** — the `mention → spawn → 👋 ack → reply → follow-up` loop (epic **ka-0000007401**; design-doc F-B). These `gardenio_jira_*` conversation counters are emitted by the jira-bridge but were charted in **no** dashboard until this board — `jira-metrics.json` is the separate JQL-count *ticket-analytics* exporter (backlog / SLA-age / throughput), not the conversation loop. Read this board top-to-bottom as the loop flows: front-half spawn/ack, reply path, follow-up warm/cold delivery, wake durability, inbound comment-mirror durability + DLQ, and the webhook deadman. All outbound writes are **deny-by-default** and gated by one shared write policy; `blocked` is a policy refusal, `error` is Jira bouncing the post. Companion boards: **Jira — Metrics** (ticket analytics) and **Inbound Webhook Liveness** (the deadman in depth). Runbook: `gardenio/docs/runbooks/jira-conversational-bridge.md`.

> ✅ **Loop counters are live.** All conversation-loop counters (`gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total`, `_spawn_ack_total`, `_reply_total`, `_followup_delivery_total`, `_followup_wake_retries_total` / `_wake_failures_total`, `_inbound_comment_write_retries_total` / `_write_failures_total`, `_inbound_comment_dlq_{enqueued,replayed,dropped,depth}`) now emit live series from the jira-bridge. The stat tiles color on threshold, so a real error rate or DLQ backlog shows orange/red. A tile reading **0** over its window is an **honest zero** — `increase()` across an idle interval is genuinely 0, not “no data”; the series exist. (Emitter landed via tracking bead **ka-0000000731**; annotation re-grounded 2026-08-19 per **ka-0000000355**.)

panels.title: Mention spawns (1h)
panels.description: sum(increase(gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total[1h])): fresh @gardenio-mention agent spawns (all outcomes) in the last hour — conversation starts.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total series — no @gardenio mention has spawned an agent since the jira-bridge booted, so the counter does not exist. Legitimate on a quiet hour; check “Webhook dark verdict” in the bottom row to rule out a dead inbound hook.

panels.title: Mention-spawn error ratio (1h)
panels.description: error / (ok+error) of gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total over 1h. Non-zero = @gardenio mentions arrive but the agent never boots — the conversation dies at the front half while the webhook already 200'd. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: the ratio is UNDEFINED, not 0% error: gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total returned nothing for the last hour, so the denominator is zero. This panel cannot tell an idle hour from a bridge that never ran — resolve with “Mention spawns (1h)” to the left and the webhook dark verdict below.

panels.title: Spawn-ack posted (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_spawn_ack_total{outcome="posted"} increase over 1h: the "👋 On it" note landed on the ticket — the front half of the reaction lifecycle.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_spawn_ack_total{outcome="posted"} series — no “👋 On it” note was posted since the bridge booted. Legitimate if no mention arrived; if “Mention spawns (1h)” is non-zero and this is empty, the ticket is going silent after a spawn.

panels.title: Spawn-ack blocked+error (1h)
panels.description: spawn-ack posts that were policy-blocked or errored over 1h. Non-zero = the ticket goes silent after a mention even though an agent booted.

defaults.noValue: gardenio_jira_spawn_ack_total{outcome=~"blocked|error"} returned nothing. The counter is created only on the first blocked/error outcome, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either none occurred since the bridge booted, or the bridge never ran. Resolve against “Spawn-ack posted (1h)” to the left — if that renders, the bridge is live and this really is zero.

panels.title: Mention spawns by outcome (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total split by outcome (ok/error). A rising error line is the front-half twin of the follow-up wake-failure signal below (which covers respawns only).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_mention_spawn_total series — no mention spawn has been attempted since the bridge booted, so there is no ok/error split to draw. Empty is not “zero errors”: it is “no data on either outcome”.

panels.title: Spawn-ack posts by outcome (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_spawn_ack_total by outcome (posted/blocked/error).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_spawn_ack_total series — no spawn-ack has been attempted since the bridge booted. Empty means the front half of the lifecycle never ran, not that every ack succeeded.

panels.title: Reply path — agent → ticket (gb jira reply)
Replies posted (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="posted"} increase over 1h: agent replies that landed on the bound ticket.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="posted"} series — no agent reply has landed on a bound ticket since the bridge booted. Legitimate on a quiet hour; if the blocked/error stats to the right are non-zero, replies are being attempted and rejected.

panels.title: Replies blocked (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="blocked"} increase over 1h: write-policy / bound-ticket refusals. Rising = a misconfig or a non-replyable project.

defaults.noValue: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="blocked"} returned nothing. Write-policy refusals create this counter on the first block, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either none were blocked since the bridge booted, or the bridge never ran. Resolve against “Replies posted (1h)” — if that renders, the bridge is live and this really is zero.

panels.title: Replies error (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="error"} increase over 1h: Jira bounced the post. Rising = Jira-side rejection (auth / 4xx / 5xx).

defaults.noValue: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="error"} returned nothing. Jira-side rejections create this counter on the first error, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either none occurred since the bridge booted, or the bridge never ran. Resolve against “Replies posted (1h)” — if that renders, the bridge is live and this really is zero.

panels.title: Public replies posted (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_reply_total{outcome="posted",visibility="public"}: customer-facing reply volume. Public replies are role-gated and granted to no role by default (deny-by-default) — a non-zero value here is a deliberately-granted customer-facing reply.

defaults.noValue: no public replies since the bridge booted — the expected state: public visibility is role-gated and granted to no role by default, so empty is the designed configuration, not a failure.

panels.title: Reply posts by outcome (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_reply_total by outcome (posted/blocked/error).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_reply_total series — no reply has been attempted since the bridge booted, so there is no posted/blocked/error split. Empty is “no attempts”, not “all clean”.

panels.title: Reply posts by visibility (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_reply_total by visibility (internal/public/none). internal = staff-only note (the default); public = customer-facing.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_reply_total series — no reply has been attempted since the bridge booted, so neither the internal nor the public line exists. Empty is “no attempts”, not “no public leakage”.

panels.title: Follow-up delivery — warm nudge vs cold respawn
Follow-up warm-hit ratio (30m)
panels.description: warm / (warm+cold) of gardenio_jira_followup_delivery_total over 30m — the Jira twin of the Slack warm-graft hit rate (epic ka-0000006987). warm = a live agent was nudged in place; cold = a stopped agent was respawned. Higher is better (the conversation stayed warm). Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no warm or cold follow-up deliveries in the last 30m — the ratio is UNDEFINED, not 0% warm. No follow-up comment reached a bound ticket in the window; check the delivery-by-path panel to the right.

panels.title: Follow-up delivery by path (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_followup_delivery_total by path (warm=live nudge / cold=same-name respawn / skipped=recent-spawn dedup).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_followup_delivery_total series — no follow-up comment has been delivered since the bridge booted, so there is no warm/cold/skipped split. Corroborate with “Authenticated deliveries (1h)” in the bottom row: empty there too means inbound is dark.

panels.title: Warm-hit ratio over time (30m window)
panels.description: warm / (warm+cold) over a 30m rolling window. A sustained dip means follow-ups keep landing on already-stopped agents (cold respawns), i.e. agents are despawning before the human replies. Empty-branch liveness: every `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="jira-bridge"} == 1`, so a 0 appears only while the jira-bridge exporter is actually being scraped — a dark bridge leaves the panel empty instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: no warm or cold follow-up deliveries in the range — the rolling ratio is UNDEFINED, not a 0% warm-hit rate. A sustained empty line means no follow-ups are arriving at all, which is an inbound problem, not a warm-graft problem.

panels.title: Wake durability — follow-up nudge / respawn retries
Follow-up wake retries by stage (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_followup_wake_retries_total by stage (nudge/spawn): transient-error retry attempts of a follow-up wake. Some retries are normal during a daemon rollout; a sustained high rate means the daemon is flaky on the wake path.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_followup_wake_retries_total series — no wake has needed a retry since the bridge booted. Healthy; retries are created on first transient error.

panels.title: Follow-up wake failures by stage (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_followup_wake_failures_total by stage (nudge/spawn): TERMINAL wake failures. Non-flat = follow-up comments are reaching the bead but never waking the agent (the reply is lost to the conversation even though it's mirrored).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_followup_wake_failures_total series — no TERMINAL wake failure since the bridge booted. This is the good state, but it only means something if follow-ups are actually arriving: check “Follow-up delivery by path” above.

panels.title: DLQ depth (current)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_dlq_depth: inbound comment mirrors currently queued in the durable replay DLQ after exhausting the inline retry. Steady growth = the daemon is down longer than the replay loop can drain.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_dlq_depth series — the gauge is published by the jira-bridge on every replay tick, so empty means the bridge is not reporting, NOT that the DLQ is empty. Check “Webhook dark verdict” below and up{component="jira-bridge"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: Inbound write retries by stage (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_write_retries_total by stage (add_comment/set_fields): transient retries mirroring a human follow-up comment onto the task bead.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_write_retries_total series — no comment-mirror write has needed a retry since the bridge booted. Healthy.

panels.title: Inbound write failures by stage (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_write_failures_total by stage: TERMINAL failures of the comment-mirror write. Non-flat = follow-up comments dropped from the bead conversation (they survive in Jira). A transient-class terminal failure is what enqueues to the DLQ below.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_write_failures_total series — no TERMINAL comment-mirror failure since the bridge booted. Good state; meaningful only while inbound deliveries are non-zero (bottom row).

panels.title: DLQ flow — enqueued / replayed / dropped (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of the three DLQ lifecycle counters. enqueued = a transient terminal failure parked a mirror; replayed = the replay loop drained one (recovery); dropped = permanently lost. Healthy steady state: enqueued ≈ replayed, dropped flat at 0.

defaults.noValue: none of the three DLQ lifecycle counters exist — nothing has been enqueued, replayed or dropped since the bridge booted. Healthy; the panel lights up on the first durable-replay event.

panels.title: DLQ drops by reason (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_dlq_dropped_total by reason (overflow/exhausted/nontransient/no_state). Any non-zero series is a permanently-lost follow-up comment — the exact failure the DLQ exists to prevent — annotated by why it could not be saved.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_inbound_comment_dlq_dropped_total series — no follow-up comment has been permanently lost since the bridge booted. This is the one panel where empty is unambiguously good.

panels.title: Webhook dark verdict
panels.description: gardenio_jira_webhook_dark{component="jira-bridge"}: 0 = a recent authenticated delivery kept the hook alive; 1 = no authenticated delivery within the deadman window while Jira upstream still shows activity (the hook is silently DARK — the whole inbound half is dead). Pinned to the owning component so the other bridges' always-zero series can't mask it at max().

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_webhook_dark series — the deadman monitor itself is not reporting, which is WORSE than a dark verdict of 1: nothing is watching the inbound hook. Check up{component="jira-bridge"} on Gardenio — System Health.

panels.title: Authenticated deliveries (1h)
panels.description: gardenio_jira_webhook_deliveries_total{outcome=~"processed|ignored"} increase over 1h: authenticated inbound deliveries — the receive-path liveness counter. Zero for a sustained period while upstream is active is what trips the dark verdict.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_webhook_deliveries_total series — no authenticated inbound delivery since the bridge booted, so the receive-path counter does not exist. Combined with a dark verdict of 1 this is the confirmed “hook is dead” state.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by outcome (rate/5m)
panels.description: rate() of gardenio_jira_webhook_deliveries_total by terminal outcome. processed/ignored = authenticated; hmac_failed = fail-closed 403; bad_request = malformed. A rejected-but-arriving stream shows here instead of silence. Deep-dive board: Inbound Webhook Liveness.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_jira_webhook_deliveries_total series — no inbound delivery of any outcome (processed / ignored / hmac_failed / bad_request) since the bridge booted. Empty is “nothing arrived”, not “nothing was rejected”.

panels.title: Mention cold-respawn latency — p50 / p90 / p99 (SLO 30s p95)

defaults.noValue: no cold-respawn samples in the window — either every mention hit a warm agent, or the counter is not reporting

panels.description: Wall-clock from an inbound Jira/Slack mention to a live agent for the cold path. This is the number a human actually experiences when they @-mention the bot; the dashed line is the 30s p95 SLO.

panels.title: Follow-up wake failures by stage (window)

defaults.noValue: no wake-failure samples in the window — either none failed, or the counter is not reporting

panels.description: Failure inventory for the follow-up wake path, by stage — the sortable form of the rate chart above, so a stage that fails once an hour is still visible.

panels.title: DLQ depth & drop reasons (window)

defaults.noValue: no DLQ or drop samples in the window — either nothing was dropped, or the counters are not reporting

panels.description: Current dead-letter depth next to the drop reasons accumulated over the window: depth is recoverable backlog, drops are lost inbound comments.

title: Jira — Conversation-Loop Health
description: Health of the Jira conversation loop: mention→spawn, spawn-ack, reply and follow-up delivery outcomes, warm-hit ratio, wake retries and failures, DLQ depth and drops, plus inbound webhook delivery. Open this when a Jira mention got no answer — the panels localise the break to spawn, reply, follow-up or webhook.
